Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 4 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/recording_context.py
  tests/test_recording_context_removed_spans.py
  tests/test_recording_context.py

THE BUG, proven on a real certified episode. server/pipeline/recording_context.py scans the interview transcript for release-affecting requests and emits publish_holds that BLOCK publication. It scans the WHOLE transcript, including material the edit already REMOVED, so it blocks on content that is not in the published cut.

The real case: it raised a hold of type "edit_requested" at transcript line 47 (timestamp 00:06:55) on the text "drinking it was evolved okay maybe we should take that out right uh we'll make that judgment call". Reading the surrounding lines, the host is explaining the editing POLICY to the guest before the interview begins, and the very next line says "but i don't think it will have any type of conversation like that today". More decisively: that span sits at session-grid t=415s, inside the applied cut 0-491s, and cross-correlating its audio against the finished master finds no match (r=0.070) — it is provably ABSENT from what would be published. The pipeline was therefore holding publication over words nobody can hear.

THE FIX — a hold must describe the PUBLISHED cut, not the raw recording:
1. Accept an optional removed_spans argument (a sequence of {"start_s","end_s"} dicts, the same shape as the applied-cuts receipt) on the public entry point(s) that produce holds/todos. Inspect the real signatures and thread it through; keep the parameter optional with a default of None so every existing caller keeps working unchanged.
2. Each transcript line carries a timestamp (format [HH:MM:SS] at line start, as in "[00:06:55] Host: ..."). Parse it to seconds. When a candidate hold or todo's line timestamp falls inside ANY removed span, do NOT emit it as an open blocking hold. Instead emit it with status "resolved_by_edit" and an added field removed_by_span (the span that covers it), so the record is preserved and auditable rather than silently dropped. Blocking logic must count only holds whose status is "open".
3. A line with an UNPARSEABLE or missing timestamp must be treated as SURVIVING (open) — never assume removal. State that in a comment: absence of evidence is not evidence of removal.
4. When removed_spans is None or empty, behaviour is exactly as today (every candidate open). Do not change the detection patterns themselves.

TESTS (tests/test_recording_context_removed_spans.py, pure, synthetic transcript strings; at least 4): (1) a release-affecting line whose timestamp falls inside a removed span is emitted with status "resolved_by_edit" and does NOT count as a blocking hold; (2) NEGATIVE: the SAME line with removed_spans=None (or a span that does not cover it) still produces an OPEN blocking hold — proving the fix cannot mask surviving content; (3) a line with no parseable timestamp inside an otherwise-covering span stays OPEN; (4) todos are annotated the same way and a removed todo does not appear in the open set; (5) exercise the real-world payload: a transcript line at [00:06:55] with removed span 0-491 resolves, while a line at [00:12:00] with the same span stays open.
tasks.verified: publish holds describe the PUBLISHED cut: candidates inside removed spans resolve instead of blocking, surviving ones still block

tasks.spec:
You are an implementation worker writing a NEW deterministic validator. Write exactly ONE file in your current working directory: ./voice_check.py. No repo writes, no git, no MCP, no network. Pure stdlib.

PURPOSE. A podcast owner's promo copy (LinkedIn/X posts, guest emails, show notes) is repeatedly rejected by a human-voice reviewer as "AI-written". The rejections are consistent and mechanical enough to gate deterministically BEFORE a model-based reviewer is spent. This validator is that gate. It must judge SUBSTANCE mechanically, print WHY for every failure, and never pass empty or missing content.

INPUT CONTRACT: ./voice_check.py with argparse:
  voice_check.py --content PATH [--episode-duration-s FLOAT] [--min-contraction-rate 0.004] [--json OUT]
  voice_check.py --self-test
--content is a JSON file containing the drafts. Support BOTH shapes and say which was detected: (a) {"posts": [{"platform": ..., "text": ...}, ...], "email": {"subject":..., "body":...}, "show_notes": "..."} and (b) a flat list of {"name","text"} items. Missing/empty --content, zero text items, or any item whose text is blank => exit 2 UNMEASURABLE (never a pass).
Exit 0 only when every rule passes; exit 1 on any violation; exit 2 on unusable input.

RULES (each a named constant list/threshold with a one-line rationale; report per item PASS/FAIL with the offending excerpt):
1. CONTRACTIONS: the single biggest AI tell in the rejections was zero contractions. Require contraction_rate = (count of contraction tokens) / (word count) >= --min-contraction-rate in EVERY text item over 25 words. Detect a reasonable set ("don't","isn't","he's","you're","I'm","didn't","wasn't","it's","that's","we've","they're","can't","won't","there's","here's","who's","let's","you'll","I'd","he'd" and the generic pattern of a letter followed by an apostrophe then 1-2 letters). Report the rate and the count.
2. BANNED_PHRASES: fail on any of these (case-insensitive, word-boundary aware): delve, dive into, unpack, leverage, utilize, optimize, robust, seamless, streamline, foster, cultivate, bolster, landscape, ecosystem, holistic, alignment, synergy, bandwidth, revolutionary, game-changing, cutting-edge, elevate, transform, unlock, comprehensive, passionate, "I'd be happy to", "Great question", "It's important to note", "Don't miss out", "But wait, there's more", "We're excited to", "just checking in", "circling back", "touching base", "hope this email finds you well", "I hope you're doing well", "wanted to reach out", "I came across", "your reviews tell the story", "that's on me", "my bad", "I owe you a note", "smart evolution", "no agenda here", "just wanted to say".
3. NO_EM_DASH: fail on any em dash (U+2014) or " - " used as emphasis between clauses. House rule: commas or periods instead.
4. SELF_ANSWERED_QUESTION: fail on a question immediately followed by its own one-to-three-word answer (e.g. "What made it possible? Burnout."). Detect: a sentence ending in '?' followed by a sentence of <= 3 words. This exact cadence was named in the rejections.
5. ONE_CTA: each post must contain at most ONE call to action. Count CTA signals: an imperative listen/hear/watch/check/read/tune directive, a URL or link placeholder, and a direct audience question. Fail when a single post carries more than one DISTINCT cta signal type. Report which signals were found.
6. NO_CROSS_ITEM_REUSE: across posts, fail when any normalized sentence (lowercased, punctuation stripped, whitespace collapsed) of >= 8 words appears in more than one post, or when any two posts share >= 0.5 Jaccard similarity over their >= 4-word shingles. The rejections called this "one post at three lengths". Report the duplicated sentence or the pair and score.
7. LINK_CONSISTENCY: if any post uses a link placeholder (e.g. {{episode_link}}), fail when another post substitutes prose like "Link in bio" instead — a mixed mechanism breaks templating and tracking. Report both.
8. UNSOURCED_STAT: fail on statistic-shaped claims with no number and no attribution, matching quantifier openers ("most", "the majority of", "nearly all", "hardly any", "few") followed within the sentence by a population noun and an outcome verb. The rejections flagged 'Most doctors who burn out leave optometry and don't come back.' Report the sentence and instruct the writer to hedge or cite.
9. RUNTIME_CLAIM: when --episode-duration-s is given, fail on any asserted runtime ("worth 45 minutes", "45-minute", "in 45 min") that differs from the true duration by more than RUNTIME_TOLERANCE_MIN (2 minutes). Without the flag, report SKIPPED with a WHY (never guess).
10. SENTENCE_LENGTH: fail when any item contains a sentence over MAX_SENTENCE_WORDS (38) — the rejections flagged 40+ word run-ons. Report the sentence.

SELF-TEST (--self-test, hermetic, no network): build fixtures IN CODE and assert each rule fires. Use these REAL rejected excerpts as red fixtures, each of which must trip its named rule and produce exit 1:
  - "He is now building a team of travel optometrists. He is licensed in Ontario. If you have ever struggled to cover exam lanes, this is the episode." (CONTRACTIONS: zero contractions)
  - "What made it possible? Burnout." (SELF_ANSWERED_QUESTION)
  - "Most doctors who burn out leave optometry and don't come back." (UNSOURCED_STAT)
  - "this one is worth 45 minutes" with --episode-duration-s 2218 (RUNTIME_CLAIM: true runtime is ~37 min)
  - two posts both containing "licensed in Ontario, Manitoba, and Newfoundland and building a travel optometry team" (NO_CROSS_ITEM_REUSE)
  - one post with "{{episode_link}}" and another with "Link in bio." (LINK_CONSISTENCY)
  - a post with a listen directive AND a link AND an audience question (ONE_CTA)
  - a 45-word single sentence (SENTENCE_LENGTH)
  - a post containing "leverage" and "seamless" (BANNED_PHRASES)
  - a post using an em dash for emphasis (NO_EM_DASH)
Also include a GREEN fixture: a short, contraction-rich, single-CTA, specific post set that passes every rule with exit 0 — and an empty-content fixture that exits 2. Print every measured number. Self-test exits 0 only when every red fixture is red, the green fixture is green, and the unusable fixture exits 2.
